meta.triageRationale: One cohesive story inside the VS Code plugin's chat module, with real design choices and several tasks: how an attachment reaches each CLI, where files are kept and removed, new messages and a new row field, the paste handler and attach button in the one inline shell script, and limits on size and type.

reviewOverride.reason: User override (2026-10-12): the review's findings are accepted and carried into the plan as explicit tasks. (1) Only the submit-turn caller takes the pending attachments; the grant re-run and the selection continuation pass none and only get readDirs, with a host test that both leave the pending list untouched. (2) The host's submit-turn case supersedes queued approvals when the text is non-blank OR the session has pending attachments, covered by the blank-text host test. (3) The protocol invariant is reworded to what is true: the new kinds are added to the two type lists and the protocol test asserts each by name; the lists are not exhaustive today (approval-position is missing) and this Story does not rely on that. (4) The session and its pending list are captured before the wait for in-flight attachment writes and the turn runs on that session; a chat switch or a second submit during the wait is specified and tested. Decisions recorded by the user: limits are 20 MB per file and 10 attachments per message, pasted images PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP, documents of any type; drag-and-drop and image previews in the transcript are out of scope. Codex was checked after the design was written (codex-cli 0.162.1): with only the paths in the prompt and no extra flag it answered from an image and a text file outside its working directory, so the codex argv stays unchanged.

q70a38cf1.question: How does the codex CLI take an image or a file? It is not installed on the machine this was designed on, so the design passes the attached paths in the prompt and leaves the codex argv unchanged. Options: leave as designed and verify on a machine with codex; or add a per-image flag for codex once its CLI is checked.
q70a38cf1.rationale: Already verified on 2026-10-12 with codex-cli 0.162.1 after the user installed it: with only the attached paths in the prompt and no extra flag, run from a directory that did not hold the files, it answered with the image's colour and the text file's content. Codex also has -i/--image, which the design does not need; the codex argv stays unchanged.

summary.prose: In the dev chat you can paste an image into the prompt, or press an icon-only attach button under the prompt to pick documents. Each attachment appears as a removable chip before you send, travels with the message, and is shown on your message in the transcript, where a click opens it. The files are copied into a per-chat folder under ~/.insrc/chat-attachments and the assistant is given their paths and permission to read that folder only. This is measured to work with the claude CLI; for codex the paths are passed the same way but could not be checked on this machine.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Paste images and attach documents in the dev chat prompt

api.name: TurnRequest
api.signature: interface TurnRequest { readonly provider: ProviderId; readonly prompt: string; readonly resume?: SessionHandle; readonly cwd: string; readonly permissionMode?: PermissionMode; readonly allowedTools?: readonly string[]; readonly readDirs?: readonly string[] /* NEW */ }

parameters.name: readDirs
parameters.purpose: Directories outside cwd the CLI may read this turn: the session's attachments directory when the session has any attachment.

returns.meaning: Existing type in cli-adapter.ts with one optional field added. The claude adapter's buildArgs adds `--add-dir <dir>...` before the permission flags when readDirs is non-empty; with no readDirs its argv is byte-identical to today. The codex adapter's argv is unchanged: the attached paths are in the prompt only.

postconditions: The prompt is still the last argv item after `--`.

api.name: runTurn (chat-panel.ts)
api.signature: function runTurn(text: unknown, allowedTools?: readonly string[], opts?: { readonly suppressEcho?: boolean | undefined }): Promise<void>  // existing; behaviour extended

returns.meaning: On a submit the host takes ALL pending attachments of the active session with the message. The stored user row keeps the user's own text and gains `attachments`; the prompt sent to the CLI is the text followed by a block listing each attached file's absolute path, one per line, under the line 'Attached files (read them with your file tools):'. The request carries readDirs = [the session's attachments directory] on this turn and on every later turn of a session whose transcript holds an attachment, including the synthesized grant re-runs.

preconditions: Attachments still being written when the user submits are awaited first, so a message never goes without a file the user saw as a chip.
postconditions: A submit with blank text and at least one pending attachment runs a turn; with blank text and none it is still a no-op.
After a submit the session's pending list is empty and an `attachments-pending` with no items is posted.
A first message with blank text names the chat from its first attachment's name.

api.name: WebviewToHost / HostToWebview (protocol.ts)
api.signature: NEW webview->host: { type: 'attach-image'; mime: string; dataBase64: string; name?: string; clientId?: string } | { type: 'pick-attachments' } | { type: 'remove-attachment'; attachmentId: string } | { type: 'open-attachment'; attachmentId: string }.  NEW host->webview: { type: 'attachments-pending'; sessionId: string; items: readonly PendingAttachmentView[]; error?: string }.  CHANGED host->webview: 'user-row' gains `attachments?: readonly AttachmentRef[]`.  type PendingAttachmentView = { id: string; name: string; kind: 'image' | 'file'; size: number; clientId?: string }

returns.meaning: `submit-turn` is unchanged: the host owns the pending list, so a rebuilt webview loses nothing. Every new kind is added to the two type lists the protocol test pins. No message carries a file path from the webview: attachments are named by the id the host issued.

postconditions: `attachments-pending` is posted after every add, remove and pick, after a submit, and with the session state on `ready`, new-chat and open-chat.
`error` carries one plain sentence when an attachment was refused (too large, too many, not an image, unreadable).

api.name: AttachmentStore
api.signature: NEW, in vscode-plugin/src/chat/attachment-store.ts.  interface AttachmentRef { readonly id: string; readonly name: string; readonly kind: 'image' | 'file'; readonly size: number; readonly path: string }.  interface AttachmentStore { dirOf(sessionId: string): string; addBytes(sessionId: string, input: { name: string; mime: string; bytes: Uint8Array }): Promise<AttachmentRef>; addFile(sessionId: string, sourcePath: string): Promise<AttachmentRef>; remove(sessionId: string, attachmentId: string): Promise<void>; removeSession(sessionId: string): Promise<void>; sweep(opts: { olderThanMs: number; keep: ReadonlySet<string> }): Promise<void> }.  function createAttachmentStore(deps: { root: string; fs?: AttachmentFs; logger?: { warn(msg: string): void }; now?: () => number }): AttachmentStore.  export const MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024; export const MAX_ATTACHMENTS_PER_MESSAGE = 10; export const PASTE_IMAGE_MIMES = ['image/png','image/jpeg','image/gif','image/webp']

parameters.name: deps.fs
parameters.purpose: The file seam (mkdir, writeFile, copyFile, stat, rm, readdir), node's fs/promises by default, a fake in tests, as SessionOutputFs is.

returns.meaning: Each session's attachments are files in `<root>/<sessionFileName(sessionId)>/`, named `<n>-<safe name>`; that file name is the attachment's id. A picked document is copied, never referenced in place.

errors.condition: The bytes or the source file are larger than MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES, a pasted mime is not in PASTE_IMAGE_MIMES, or the source is not a regular file. Its message is the sentence shown to the user.
A file call fails; the host shows it as the pending list's error and logs it.

postconditions: The stored name keeps only A-Za-z0-9._- from the given name, never a path separator, and a pasted image with no name is `pasted-image.<ext from mime>`.
remove() and removeSession() succeed when the file or directory is already gone; remove() ignores an id that is not a plain file name in that session's directory.
sweep() removes the directories of sessions not in `keep` whose every file is older than olderThanMs, as the output sweep does.

api.name: ChatPanelHostDeps
api.signature: interface ChatPanelHostDeps { ...existing; readonly attachments?: { readonly store: AttachmentStore; pickFiles(): Promise<readonly string[]>; open(path: string): void } /* NEW */ }

parameters.name: attachments
parameters.purpose: The attachment store and the two VS Code seams (the file dialog and opening a file), injected by extension.ts so chat-panel.ts stays free of the vscode module.

returns.meaning: Without `attachments` the shell renders no attach button and no chip row, pasting an image does nothing, and the four new messages are ignored: today's behaviour exactly.

preconditions: vscode-plugin/src/vscode.d.ts, the plugin's own declaration of the vscode module, gains `window.showOpenDialog(options: { canSelectMany?: boolean; openLabel?: string }): PromiseLike<readonly Uri[] | undefined>`; it already declares Uri.file and commands.executeCommand.
postconditions: extension.ts builds the store on join(PATHS.insrc, 'chat-attachments'); passes pickFiles, which calls vscode.window.showOpenDialog with canSelectMany and returns the chosen files' fsPath values (none when the dialog is dismissed); passes open, which runs commands.executeCommand('vscode.open', Uri.file(path)); removes a session's attachments in the store's onEvict beside its output files; and sweeps at start with the same keep set and age as the output sweep.

dataModelChanges.details: The user row gains `attachments?: readonly AttachmentRef[]`, absent when the message had none, so every existing row and every message without attachments is stored exactly as today. The file store already carries a field it does not know, so nothing in the store changes. `text` stays the user's own words; the path block exists only in the prompt sent to the CLI.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: { role: 'user', text, at }  ->  { role: 'user', text, at, attachments?: [{ id, name, kind, size, path }] }

dataModelChanges.details: One directory per session holding the copied files. It is the only path given to the CLI as readDirs. Removed when its session is evicted; a directory no session keeps (a draft never sent, or pending files lost at a window reload) is removed by the start-up sweep once its files are older than the sweep's age.

Per session id, in the panel host: the AttachmentRefs added since the last submit, in order, at most MAX_ATTACHMENTS_PER_MESSAGE. Kept across a webview rebuild and a chat switch within the window; lost at a window reload. Adds are serialized per session and a submit waits for them.

When attachments are enabled: `.statusbar` gains, as its first item, an icon-only button `#insrc-attach` (an inline SVG paperclip, aria-label and title 'attach files') that posts pick-attachments; a chip row `#insrc-attachments` sits between `.inputbar` and `.statusbar`, hidden while empty, each chip showing a kind glyph, the name, the size and a remove control, built with textContent only; a paste on `#insrc-input` whose clipboard holds image items posts one attach-image per image and is prevented, while a text paste is untouched; doSubmit also submits when the box is blank and chips are shown. A pasted image's chip shows a thumbnail from the data: URL the webview already holds (allowed by the existing `img-src data:`), matched by clientId; after a rebuild it shows the glyph. The content security policy is not changed.

toViewModel, in both its host and webview copies, carries `attachments` on a user row, and the user row renders them as chips under the text (kind glyph, name, size; textContent only, no image is loaded). The registry gains a callback setter `onAttachmentOpen(cb)` beside onApprovalDecision and onSelectionDecision, returned on the registry object; a click on a chip calls it with the attachment's id, and the shell wires it to post open-attachment. The host resolves the id against the active session's rows and pending list and opens that file; an unknown id does nothing.
`namespace window` gains showOpenDialog, the only VS Code call this Story uses that the plugin's declaration does not have yet.

errorCases.scenario: A pasted image or a picked file is larger than the limit.
errorCases.detection: For a paste, the base64 text's length times 3/4 exceeds MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES before it is decoded; for a file, stat's size exceeds it before any copy.
errorCases.response: Nothing is written. The pending list is posted unchanged with an error sentence naming the file and the limit.
errorCases.userImpact: The chip does not appear and a line under the prompt says why.

errorCases.scenario: More than MAX_ATTACHMENTS_PER_MESSAGE attachments are added to one message.
errorCases.detection: The session's pending list is already at the limit when an add arrives, or a pick returns more files than the remaining room.
errorCases.response: Files are taken in order up to the limit; the rest are refused with one error sentence giving the limit.
errorCases.userImpact: The first ten are attached; the user is told the others were not.

errorCases.scenario: A pasted item is not an allowed image type, or its base64 does not decode.
errorCases.detection: The message's mime is not in PASTE_IMAGE_MIMES, or the decoded length is zero or disagrees with the text's length.
errorCases.response: Refused with an error sentence; nothing is written.
errorCases.userImpact: No chip; a line says the pasted item is not a supported image.

errorCases.scenario: A picked path is not a readable regular file.
errorCases.detection: stat fails or reports a directory or another kind of file; copyFile fails.
errorCases.response: That file is refused with an error sentence naming it; the other picked files are still attached.
errorCases.userImpact: One file is missing from the chips, with the reason shown.

errorCases.scenario: Writing an attachment fails (disk full, directory not writable).
errorCases.response: The error is logged and posted as the pending list's error; a partly written file is removed; the pending list is unchanged.
errorCases.userImpact: The attachment is not added and the user sees why.

errorCases.scenario: The file dialog fails or is dismissed.
errorCases.detection: pickFiles rejects, or resolves with no path.
errorCases.response: A rejection is logged and posted as the pending list's error; a dismissal changes nothing and posts nothing.
errorCases.userImpact: None for a dismissal; an error line for a failure.

errorCases.scenario: An attached file is gone when the turn runs or when a chip is clicked.
errorCases.detection: For a click, the host's stat of the resolved path fails; for a turn, the CLI's own read fails.
errorCases.response: A click logs and does nothing. A turn is still sent with the path listed; the assistant reports it could not read the file.
errorCases.userImpact: The message is sent; the assistant says the file is missing.

errorCases.scenario: A message names an attachment id the host did not issue.
errorCases.detection: remove-attachment or open-attachment carries an id that is not a string, or matches no pending attachment and no row of the active session.
errorCases.response: Ignored; no file call is made with a path built from the message.

errorCases.scenario: Removing an evicted session's attachments, or the start-up sweep, fails.
errorCases.response: Logged; the eviction and the start-up carry on, as they do for the output files.
errorCases.userImpact: None; a stale directory may remain until the next sweep.

edgeCases.input: A submit with blank text and one pending attachment.
edgeCases.expected: A turn runs; the user row has empty text and the attachment; the prompt is the attached-files block alone.

edgeCases.input: A paste that holds both text and an image.
edgeCases.expected: The image is attached and the text paste is prevented; a paste with only text behaves as today.

edgeCases.input: Two images pasted in quick succession, then a submit before the second is written.
edgeCases.expected: The submit waits for both; the message carries both, in paste order.

edgeCases.input: A picked file whose name has spaces, unicode or path separators.
edgeCases.expected: Stored under a name of A-Za-z0-9._- characters with a numeric prefix; the chip and the row show the original file name.

invariantsToPreserve.text: The prompt is the last argv item after `--` for both CLIs, and with no readDirs each argv is byte-identical to today.
A submit with blank text and nothing attached is a no-op; a malformed submit never throws.
The shell stays one nonce'd inline script under the same content security policy, builds text with textContent, and loads nothing from a remote origin.
chat-panel.ts does not import the vscode module; VS Code is reached only through injected seams.
Every message kind is named in the protocol's type lists, and an unknown inbound message is ignored.
A stored row is plain JSON, existing rows keep their exact shape, and the transcript is only pushed to.
A live user row and its replay reconcile to one rendered row by its key; the host and webview copies of toViewModel agree.
An evicted session's files are removed and stale files are swept at start, failures logged and not thrown.

migration.stateBefore: A turn is a prompt string only: the webview sends submit-turn with text, the user row stores text, and each CLI gets the prompt as its last argv item (s1: how a turn's prompt reaches each CLI; s1: the message protocol and the stored user row). The prompt area has a send control, a textarea and a status bar with two selects (s1: the shell's prompt area).
migration.stateAfter: A message can carry attachments. They are files in the chat's own directory under ~/.insrc/chat-attachments, listed on the stored user row, named by path in the prompt, and readable by the claude CLI through --add-dir. The prompt area has an attach button in the status bar and a chip row. Chats and messages without attachments are stored and sent exactly as before.

migrationSteps.action: Add the attachment store and the optional readDirs field with the claude flag. Nothing calls them yet; every existing argv is unchanged.
Add the new message kinds and the optional attachments field on the user row and the user-row echo. Old rows have no such field and read as before.
Add the host handling behind the optional attachments seams and the row chips in the renderer. With the seams absent nothing changes.
Add the attach button, the chip row and the paste handling to the shell, shown only when the seams are present.
Declare showOpenDialog in the plugin's vscode declaration, inject the seams in extension.ts, remove a session's attachments on eviction and sweep them at start. From here the feature is on.

migration.backwardCompat: Additive only. submit-turn is unchanged; TurnRequest, the user row and user-row gain optional fields; ChatPanelHostDeps gains an optional member. A session written by this version and opened by an older one shows its messages without the chips, since the older renderer ignores the extra field, and the attachment files stay on disk. No stored data is rewritten.

alternativesConsidered.name: Copy into a per-session attachments directory and hand the CLI paths
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Every pasted image and picked document is copied to ~/.insrc/chat-attachments/<session>/, and the turn's prompt names those paths with the directory allowed for the CLI.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new host-side attachment store keeps each session's attachments as files in its own directory. A pasted image travels from the webview to the host as base64 in a message; a document is chosen in VS Code's own file dialog, opened by the host, and copied in. The host holds the pending list for the session and shows it as removable chips under the prompt. On submit the user row stores the attachments beside the text, and the prompt sent to the CLI is the user's text followed by a short list of the attached paths. TurnRequest gains the directories to allow; the claude adapter passes them with --add-dir.
pros: Measured to work with the claude CLI for an image and a text file.
Only one directory per session is opened to the CLI, never the folder a document came from.
An attachment stays readable in later turns and after the original is moved or edited.
The prompt is still one argv item; the stored row carries the new field with no migration.
cons: Each attachment is copied, so it uses disk until its session is evicted.
The model reads a file through its own tools, so a file type the CLI cannot read is only a path to it.
How codex takes images could not be checked on this machine.

alternativesConsidered.name: Reference documents in place
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Pasted images are saved as in a1, but a picked document is not copied: its own path goes into the prompt and its folder is allowed.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The same messages and row shape as a1, except that a document chosen in the file dialog is recorded by its original path. The directories allowed for the CLI are the attachments directory plus the parent folder of every referenced document.
pros: The model sees the document's current content on every turn.
cons: Allowing a document's parent folder opens everything else in that folder to the CLI's read tools.
A moved or deleted document breaks an old message's attachment.
Two kinds of attachment with different lifetimes to clean up.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Saves a copy at the price of exposing whole folders and of attachments that break when the original moves.

alternativesConsidered.name: Send content inline over the CLI's streaming input
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Run the claude CLI with --input-format=stream-json and send the image bytes and document text inside the user message.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Change the claude adapter to write the turn to the CLI's standard input as a stream-json user message whose content holds image and text blocks, instead of passing a prompt argument. Attachments are still kept on disk for the transcript, but the model receives them inline.
pros: The image is in the model's context at once, with no tool call to read it.
No directory has to be allowed.
cons: Replaces the argv contract every claude turn uses today, including resume, the permission flags and the grant re-run.
Nothing equivalent is known for codex, so the two providers would diverge.
Large documents inline cost context on every turn; binary documents cannot be sent this way.
Not probed; the exact input schema would have to be established first.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: The most direct delivery to the model, but unproven, claude-only and a rewrite of how every turn is started.

openQuestions: How does the codex CLI take an image or a file? It is not installed on the machine this was designed on, so the design passes the attached paths in the prompt and leaves the codex argv unchanged. Options: leave as designed and verify on a machine with codex; or add a per-image flag for codex once its CLI is checked.
